cards.explanation: The word is suppress. Paul, the apostle (Romans 1:1) writing this letter to believers in Rome (Romans 1:7), says these are men "…who suppress the truth by their wickedness." You know that move where you hold a beach ball underwater? It takes effort, and it keeps wanting to pop right back up. The truth is right there, friends, and they're sitting on it.

The answer is True. Paul says, "For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them." Notice who does the making plain. It isn't people figuring it out on their own. God did it.

The word is workmanship. Paul says God's invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, are "…understood from His workmanship…" His qualities are invisible, but what He made can be seen. It's like how you can tell a lot about a cook from one look at the cookie tray.

The answer is that they are without excuse, exactly as Paul says. God's invisible qualities "…have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse." Clearly seen leaves very little room for "I had no idea." It's like telling the boss you had no idea the report was due when it's been on your calendar in red.
The answer is False. Paul says, "…although they knew God…" So the problem wasn't that they never knew Him. They knew Him and still didn't glorify Him as God or give thanks.

The answer is futile thinking and darkened hearts. Paul says "…they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts." Futile means it goes nowhere. Think of a hamster wheel that's very busy and very sure of itself, friends.

The answer is images of mortal man and animals. Paul says they "…exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles." Look at the two sides of that trade, bakers. On one side is the immortal God, and on the other are images of things that die.

The answer is that God gives them over to impurity. The text says, "Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another." This is a heavy verse, and I think it's meant to be. Notice the words: God gave them over.

The word is creature. Paul says they "…worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator…" Those two words look a lot alike, but there's one big difference. It's like swapping the person who baked your cookies for the cookie.

The answer is True. Paul says the Creator "…is forever worthy of praise! Amen." Right in the middle of a heavy passage, he stops to say that. Some things get said out loud no matter what else is going on, friends.

The answer is a depraved mind. Paul says, "…since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind…" It's a heavy phrase, and I think it's meant to land that way. The verse ties the giving up to their not acknowledging God.
The answer is True. Paul says God gave them up to a depraved mind, "…to do what ought not to be done." That's just what the verse says. The depraved mind and the doing sit in the same sentence.
The answer is False. In his list Paul writes, "They invent new forms of evil…" So the text says they do invent new ones. That's quite a list to be on, bakers.

The answer is that they keep going and approve of others. Paul says, "…they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them." Knowing the decree didn't stop them. They kept going and approved of those who practice these things, which is a hard thing to read, friends.
